ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancellation case in which the driver asserts a rider no-show, so it enters through NS-0's driver-branch and is decided by NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. The driver did arrive: his closest approach was 3 m at 21:29:20 and he tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:45 while 41 m from the pickup, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are satisfied [F1][F6][NS-1].

The controlling element is NS-1 (iii): more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting inside the pickup radius after the arrival confirmation. The platform/timeline record caps the wait at 2 min 55 s inside 200 m before cancellation (arrival recorded 21:28:35, cancellation 21:31:30), and only 1 min 45 s elapsed inside 200 m after the 21:29:45 tap — both below the >180 s the clause requires [F2][F5][F6][F4][NS-1]. The pre-tap interval cannot be added in, and the driver's own post-hoc statement of "at least 5 minutes" is a statement contradicted by the gps/timeline records, which prevail [F12][F2][F5][NS-1]. Being stationary at 39 m from 21:29:25 to 21:31:30 confirms presence but does not extend the statutory clock [F3][NS-1].

With (iii) unmet, NS-1 fails and NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee has no basis and is refunded in full [F7][F4][NS-2]. The amount is the recorded cancellation fee of $6.61 with no surge component (multiplier 1.0×), and the sum is fixed by the fare record rather than a per-km computation because this is a flat cancellation fee, not metered distance [F7][F8][NS-0].

No account flag attaches: the "I'm Here" tap was made 41 m from the pickup, i.e. inside the arrival range, so NS-2's flag condition for a confirmation made outside the pickup range is not triggered [F6][NS-2]; and neither party's history shows a repeated upheld-violation pattern (rider 0/0; driver 1 dispute, 0 upheld in 90 d, but this case is not upheld against a prior upheld matter) so RD-6's "repeated" precondition is not met on this record [F16][F17][RD-6]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped, the two messages being the 21:29 arrival notice and the 21:31 cancellation notice; nothing about the environment (no incidents, no speed bands, fair weather) excuses or aggravates the shortfall [F9][F10][F11][F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

Safety screen: I read the chat (arrival notice and cancellation notice), the driver's written statement, and the rider's complaint. They contain a waiting-time grievance only — no threat, intimidation, harassment, unwanted sexual advance, or dangerous-driving allegation. Nothing to escalate on this ground [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted only so far as it goes; arrival satisfies NS-1 (i)/(ii) but not (iii), which the record caps at 105 s after the tap [F6][NS-1].
Being stationary 39 m from the pickup (F3) shows presence, not the >3 min post-tap wait NS-1 (iii) requires; F6 gives only 105 s [F3][F6][NS-1].
Correct that the fee stands or falls on NS-1, but on that test it falls: 2 min 55 s inside 200 m and 105 s after the tap, so NS-2 refunds the $6.61 [F2][F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2].
The complete timestamped chat (F9, F10, F11) confirms rather than defeats the short wait — fewer than 3 minutes elapse between the arrival notice and the cancellation notice [F9][F10][F11][NS-1].
Good faith and genuine presence (F1, F3) do not satisfy NS-1 (iii), a hard requirement; the $6.61 is therefore not payable [F2][F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2].
NS-0 routes a driver-cancellation case where the driver claims no-show into NS-1/NS-2, not NS-3; the refund rests on NS-2, though the result the rider seeks is correct [F4][NS-0][NS-2][NS-3].
The rider's profile (F16) is not needed and cannot itself decide the case; the wait test is settled by the gps/timeline records [F16][F2][F6][NS-1].
